narrative.overview:
The AK820 itself carries the screen. Its own colorway (black case, light-ash alphas, dark-ash modifiers, mustard Esc, Enter and Space) is drawn large and central, and the rest of the app is a quiet light-ash workroom around it: white panels on an ash ground, ink type, one stroke of Lucide line icons. The interface borrows its only accent from the yellow keycaps, and spends it where the keycaps would: on what is selected and on the one action that sends changes to the keyboard.

Density is that of a settings tool, not a dashboard, and the main pages fit one window: a 248px sidebar, a stage with the board and its status row, then compact one-line effect tiles with a row of profile chips beneath them, beside a 320px controls panel. Nothing on Lighting or Profiles scrolls the page at 1440 by 900 or 1366 by 768; the board shrinks with the viewport height instead. The developer surfaces (capture log, wire-format inspector, settings, calibration and mode-name dialogs) speak the same language at a denser grain: soft-ash tables with sticky headers and mono cells, list rows, setting rows, and native modal dialogs. Depth is soft and ambient; the only dramatic shadow belongs to the physical board. Motion is purposeful: the board's legends and underglow take the current lighting colour and cross-fade when it changes, and the board lights up once when you connect or explore. The system refuses the dark gamer dashboard and the wall of flat tabs.
keyCharacteristics: The rendered keyboard is the hero on every lighting and key surface.
Ash neutrals, ink text, mustard as the single accent; green and red appear only as status washes.
System UI face; mono only for hex, packets, capture data, mode numbers and shortcuts.
Lucide line icons at one stroke weight (1.9).
Soft, keycap-like radii stepping from 4px chips to 16px panels; soft ambient shadows.
Explicit Apply: changes are staged, the status row says so, mustard sends them.
One window: Lighting and Profiles fit the viewport without page scroll.

rules.name: The Keycap Rule
rules.body: Mustard is used the way the yellow caps are: on the selected thing and the one primary action. A screen or dialog carries one mustard-filled button; a destructive confirmation carries none.

rules.name: The Board Owns Its Colours Rule
rules.body: Case, cap, legend and knob colours live on the keyboard render only; UI chrome never borrows Case Black as a surface.

rules.name: The Wash Rule
rules.body: Status colour never fills at full strength in chrome: green and red appear as a pale wash with a darker edge and dark ink; full-strength green is reserved for dots, icons and direction markers.

rules.name: The Native Face Rule
rules.body: No display face. Hierarchy comes from weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 650 / 700) and size, not from a second family.

rules.name: The One Window Rule
rules.body: On desktop sizes (1366 by 768 and up) Lighting and Profiles never scroll the page. When space runs short, the board shrinks and lists scroll inside their panels.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: Only the keyboard casts a deep shadow on the page. UI surfaces stay at the panel shadow or flat; floating layers and modal dialogs lift above the page, never alongside the board's shadow on the same plane.

dos: Do keep the keyboard render visible and central on lighting and key surfaces.
Do spend mustard only on selection and the single primary action (The Keycap Rule).
Do stage changes and state them ("Not sent yet") until the user presses Apply; keep Apply in the status row above the board.
Do fit Lighting and Profiles in one window; shrink the board and scroll inside panels before the page ever scrolls (The One Window Rule).
Do use Lucide line icons at the shared 1.9 stroke, 16px in chrome, 18px on tiles, 20px in toasts, 12 to 14px inside pills, chips, markers and status cells.
Do show status as a pale wash with dark ink (The Wash Rule).
Do keep inapplicable controls in place, dimmed in a disabled fieldset with a reason, rather than hiding them.
Do use the native dialog for modal tasks and confirmations, with one primary action in its action bar.
Do write toast messages as a short title and a detail line.
Do ease every state change with cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) and honour reduced-motion.
Do use mono only for hex, packets, mode numbers and shortcuts.
donts: Don't turn the app into a dark gamer dashboard or a wall of flat tabs.
Don't add a second accent hue; status colours report state and are never decoration.
